newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Opposition election victory restored in Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: Opposition election victory restored in Belgrade.

text.p: The Belgrade city election commission on Tuesday decided to award victory to an opposition coalition in the city's assembly, overruling earlier decisions by the district court.
"Today we decided to annul 45 rulings of the district court," Radomir Lazarovic, head of the city elections commission, told a news conference.

"This means we have practically restored the situation with the results as found on November 17," he said. Those results awarded 60 seats to the opposition coalition and 23 to the incumbent leftist bloc among the 110 seats contested.

The ruling Socialist Party's subsequent decision to annul the municipal election outcome in Belgrade and 13 other cities triggered mass opposition protests now in their eighth straight week, challenging autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic.
Lazarovic cautioned that the results remained preliminary and the city assembly could not be constituted until they were declared official after appeal deadlines expired.
"There is no sensation in our decision (today)," he insisted. "There were no pressures or blackmail. We adhered to the law to protect the basic rights of the citizens."
